subject: On-prem readiness: capacity floor, GPU burst lanes, and PV lifecycle
messages:

Subject: On-prem capacity sync / PV lifecycle question

Dylan —

Thanks again for the walkthrough last week. We’re starting our internal checklist to make sure the private deploy meets our operational constraints before we commit to the Dedicated plan. Two quick items that would help unblock us this week:  

1) Capacity floor: we need guidance on a minimum node footprint that will keep inference latency within the SLA when we have steady-state traffic (~200 qps, 10–20 tokens average). We run mixed GPU (A10G) and CPU-backed workers today and want to avoid noisy neighbor impacts.

2) PV lifecycle & reclamation: our infra team wants a recommended lifecycle for model PVCs (ephemeral vs retained), snapshot cadence, and safe reclamation windows to avoid serving interruptions during model rollouts. Any sample retention policy or kube-side lifecycle hooks you’ve seen work well?

I’ve copied ops-eng for visibility. If you can share a short recommendation and any template configs (node profiles, storageClass knobs) that would be golden.

Thanks —
Lucas
Head of Platform, EdgeWave Systems
[ops-eng@edgewave.com]

From: dylan_brooks@redwood.com
To: Lucas Moreno <lucas.moreno@edgewave.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, sean_gallagher@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 19 Jan 2026 11:18:00 -0800
Subject: Re: On-prem capacity sync / PV lifecycle question

Hi Lucas —

Appreciate the clear ask. High-level answers up front, then a short plan we can follow together:  

- Capacity floor: for ~200 qps with 10–20 tokens avg we recommend a small baseline pool of 3 inference nodes with A10G (or equivalent) dedicated to critical low-latency routes, plus 2 CPU-backed emergent workers for administrative and batch tasks. That gives headroom for KV cache warms and one node failure without SLA violation. If you anticipate frequent model swaps, consider enabling a single extra burst lane (1 A10G) for short-lived warm-ups.

- PV lifecycle: our standard is model storage to use two classes: ephemeral tmp-pv (fast local SSD or local NVMe) for hot KV/cache and weights during inference, and retained-pv (replicated NFS/CSI backed) for canonical model artifacts and snapshots. Snapshot cadence: daily incremental, weekly full snapshot (retain 30 days) is a pragmatic starting point. Reclamation window: we recommend marking PVCs candidates for reclamation 72 hours after de-registration and a final sweep at 14 days; automated reclamation requires app-level drain/evict hooks to prevent in-flight inference loss.

Plan: I’ll draft a short config template for node pools + storage classes and attach it. Marissa — can you add the node-size recommendations and eviction tuning? Sean — please flag anything on eviction thresholds / cluster-level QoS that would affect the plan.

We can target a synchronous call Wednesday to walk the template with your ops team. Is 10am PT ok?

Cheers,
Dylan Brooks
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Lucas / team —

Adding a bit more technical detail on node pools and eviction behavior we use in on-prem deployments:  

Node pool recommendations (example tiers):
- control-plane-safe (3x m6i-type / small CPU): control plane + small infra pods (metrics, logging aggregator).
- inference-dedicated (3x A10G-equivalent): reserved for 99p latency-sensitive routes; set node taints: inference=reserved:NoSchedule.
- inference-burst (1x A10G equivalent): no long-running pods; use K8s podTopologySpread + tolerations to allow short-lived warmers.
- cpu-batch (2x c6i-type): offload heavy batch tasks and async reranks.

Storage classes and lifecycle knobs:
- sc-ephemeral-local (local-ssd, reclaimPolicy=Delete, volumeBinding=WaitForFirstConsumer): use for KV caches and ephemeral model shards.
- sc-retained-raid (CSI, reclamation=Retain, replication=2): canonical model artifacts, snapshots. Snapshot policy: Velero for daily incremental + weekly full to an internal S3 (retention 30d).

Eviction / QoS tuning:
- kubelet evictionHard: memory.available<200Mi, nodefs.available<1Gi; set evictionMinimumReclaim to protect /var/lib/modelstore (larger than defaults).
- Use PDBs for inference services during rollout: minAvailable=2 so rolling redeploys keep capacity.
- Graceful termination: ensure preStop hook drains in-flight requests (modelserver supports drain endpoint) and set terminationGracePeriodSeconds to 120.

Attachment includes a sample PV lifecycle diagram and a CSV of node sizes. A few gotchas from prior installs: local-ssd improves token latency but complicates snapshotting; we typically move canonical weights to retained RAID for backups and only keep a warmed copy on local-ssd for 6–12 hours post-rollout.

I’m attaching a short recommended retention policy + a sample Velero schedule. Happy to walk through the YAML on the call.

Marissa Cole
Sr. Infrastructure PM, Redwood Inference
